## Design hard rules — never violate these

- **Colored borders are allowed.** (Updated 2026-07-19 — reverses the earlier blanket ban.) Colored borders on cards/sections/elements are fine.
- **Side/left accent bars only on square-cornered elements.** A colored left/side accent stripe (`border-l-4`, etc.) is OK **only when the element has no border-radius**. Never put a side accent bar on a rounded (`rounded-*`) element — a colored bar clashing with a rounded corner is the look to avoid. Dots, icons, and background tints remain good status signals but are no longer mandatory substitutes.
- **A region that reads as a destination must BE one.** (2026-09-01, from the human: *"it's also not clickable in places where you'd expect it to be. i think some other views have this problem too."*) A card header carrying an object's name, or a list row with a hover fill, is an affordance; if only a few characters of it navigate, it is a broken one.
  - The pattern is `.tap-zone` / `.tap-link` in `app.css`. The region gets `.tap-zone`, the ONE anchor that owns its primary destination gets `.tap-link`, and that anchor's `::after` covers the region. Every other control inside is raised above the overlay automatically and stays clickable.
  - **Never wrap the region in an `<a>`.** It nests interactive elements inside the row's existing links and buttons, which is invalid and doubles the tab stops.
  - `Card` takes `titleHref` for the header case.
  - The trade: text inside a tap zone is not selectable except inside the raised controls. Do not put one around prose meant to be copied.
- **`.tap-link` is class-based, so the primary control does not have to be an `<a>`.** A `<button>` takes it too, which is how rollout detail's `/history` rows keep click-to-expand instead of becoming a navigation.
- **Applied:** `/environments` card headers and app rows, `/envs/<name>` "Running now" rows, `/activity` event rows, `/namespaces/<name>` rollout rows, `ActivityRail` rows, `/versions` list rows (live, no-longer-running **and** never-deployed), rollout detail `/history` rows, `/apps` app rows. **Still unfixed:** none known. `/`, `/rollouts`, `/apps/<name>`'s commit spine and `/dependencies` are already whole-block anchors and are fine.
- **Three hand-rolled overlays were found and replaced, each broken a different way** — an `after:absolute after:inset-0` pair drawing its ring inside a `truncate` box (`overflow:hidden` clips it on all four sides), and twice an invisible `<a class="absolute inset-0">` with an `aria-label`, i.e. a focus ring around an unreadable rectangle. If you are about to write one, use `.tap-zone`.
- **A `role="button"` wrapper around a row that contains links is a keyboard bug, not just a semantics one.** On `/history` it swallowed Enter: the keydown bubbled from the version link to the wrapper's handler, which called `preventDefault()` and cancelled the link's own activation. The link had a `stopPropagation` workaround; both are gone.
- **The rank badge is COLOURED on both halves, and the deviation channel is HUE.** (2026-09-02, from the human: *"i thought about newest / behind badges to use more prominent colors, not these faint / no colors."* Fourth ruling in the same direction.) Measured on `DESIGN.md`'s own `area × chroma` formula, canvas-resolved against the composited card on `/rollouts` at 1440, the wash/block pair that shipped that morning scored **24.8 / 26.3 light and 66.8 / 65.6 dark — 1.06× and 0.98×**: the deviation was not louder than the norm on the colour instrument at all, only DARKER. For scale the quietest identity chip on the same row, `DEV`, scores 54.9.
  - **⛔ THE FIRST ATTEMPT SHIPPED AS TEAL + `blue-800` AND LASTED AN HOUR.** The human named both faults on sight: *"why is behind purple? and why is newest this weird tint and not plain green?"* Measured, both are exact: `teal-700` is OKLCH **h 186.4°** against plain green's **150.1°** — the word was **36° toward cyan** — and Tailwind's `blue` ramp is violet-leaning (`blue-800` **h 265.6° at C 0.199**), which at chip scale reads purple. **A hue nobody can name cannot carry a meaning.** Both had been arrived at by DODGING an adjacency rather than designing one.
  - `newest`/`head` → **`green-800` on `green-50`** / `green-300` on `green-950/30`. Plain green. The hand-picked `#426d64` / `#83b0a8` are retired.
  - `rank` (`N behind`) → **`orange-950` ink on an `orange-100` ground** / `orange-300` on `orange-950/70`. **The hue space is CLOSED BY ELIMINATION and must not be reopened.** Four spellings were rejected in one day: loud neutral gray text (*"faint / no colors"*), `blue-800` (*"why is behind purple?"* — Tailwind's `blue` is violet-leaning at h 265.6°), `sky-800` (*"i think it shouldn't be blue"*), and a filled slate slab (*"white/black fill for behind is an eye-sore"*). Green is `newest`'s, red is adverse and behind is not adverse, amber IS `stuck`, violet is STAGING and cyan is TEST. Orange at h ~70° is what remains, and the human proposed it unprompted.
  - **⭐ HUE ANSWERS "DOES THIS NEED A PERSON". WEIGHT ANSWERS "HOW LOUD".** Being behind is a MEASUREMENT, not a verdict — drift is the pipeline's normal state, so most rollouts are behind most of the time, and what makes it matter is *why* (stuck, blocked, waiting), which already owns amber and red.
  - **A filled slate slab measured better than everything else and was still wrong** (3.84× the norm on weight, a 3.43× alarm lead on chroma). Measuring well is not the same as being right — look at it.
  - **Hold orange apart from its two warm neighbours by TREATMENT and SATURATION, never by walking the hue.** The `alarm` fill is `#ffb900` (C 0.189) and the `PROD` seed is `#d97706`. Shipped dE00 from this chip's ground: **23.6 / 32.5 light, 70.3 / 44.9 dark**; tightest figure anywhere is 7.7 (its pale ground vs `PROD`'s paler one in light, where `PROD` is *outlined* in `amber-200` and this is a neutral hairline). Two candidates died here: **`orange-900` ink is dE00 4.5 from `PROD`'s `amber-900` ink** (they are adjacent halves of one box on `/apps` — the collision that moved `rank` off amber originally), and **`orange-300` as a ground scores 242.2 on `area × chroma`, louder than `alarm` itself**; `orange-200` reads as amber-that-is-not-stuck when screenshotted beside a real `STUCK` chip.
  - **SOLVE A GREEN-ON-GREEN ADJACENCY BY TREATMENT AND LIGHTNESS, NEVER BY LEAVING GREEN.** `newest` sits beside a `Succeeded` disc (hue ~150) and, on DEV rows, a green identity chip. **`green-700` is unusable because it IS those two values** — `PRESET_RAMPS.dev.textColor` is `#008236` and so is `green-700`, dE00 **0.0** against both, at only 4.72:1. **`green-800` is 9.9 from both** (~4× the 2.3 JND), separated on LIGHTNESS (L 0.447 vs 0.530) — the axis `STATUS_DOT_CLASS` already splits settled states on — and its contrast is **6.81:1**. `emerald-700` was measured as the fallback and loses on every axis (dE 9.0, CR 5.09, lower chroma, 13.6° off green).
  - **Contrast is where the headroom went: 13.65:1 light / 9.28:1 dark**, the highest of any rank tone. (`sky-700` on `sky-200` missed the 4.5 floor by 0.10 two spellings ago — measure before falling in love with a candidate.)
  - ⚠️ **Honest residue:** `newest`'s `green-50` fill is dE00 **1.5** from the `DEV` chip's surface — they share a ground, and only the border (`gray-200` hairline vs `green-300` ring), the ink lightness and the word separate them. Do NOT "fix" it by deepening the fill: `green-100` measures presence 106 against `N behind`'s 154 and collapses the deviation ratio to 1.37×.
  - `failing`/`diverged`/`blocked` → light ground stepped **`red-50` → `red-100`**, because a merely-trailing chip must not out-ink a diverged one. Dark unchanged (`red-950/50`; its contrast argument still holds).
  - **`ADVERSE` is back at its settled `red-50`.** It stepped to `red-100` for one hour only because a chromatic blue `behind` was out-inking `diverged`; that cause expired with the blue. A change whose reason has expired is reverted, not kept.
  - Ordering, `area × chroma` (light raw; dark corrected for the chromatic card ground — every chip on `gray-800` scores its own area × 0.0335 for free and these boxes differ in area by 1.7×): light **alarm 218.6 > adverse 117.6 > `N behind` 99.7 > `newest` 70.7**; dark **130.0 > 108.9 > 91.9 > 54.2**. It holds in both themes for the first time in five spellings. `alarm` leads 2.19× / 1.41× and keeps the only saturated FILL.
  - ⚠️ **The presence ratio is CAPPED BY that ordering, and it is arithmetic.** With `newest` at 70.7 and `adverse` at 117.6, a `behind` that stays under `adverse` can be at most **1.66×** the norm on chroma. Shipped 1.41× light / 1.70× dark on chroma, 1.65× / 1.28× on `area × (chroma + |ΔL|)`. The 2.05× the blue pair reached was only available because that pair out-inked `diverged`, which is worse. A future pass wanting a bigger ratio must move `newest` down or `adverse` up — not this chip.
  - Adjacency, canvas-resolved: `newest` vs DEV ink **9.9 light / 9.1 dark**, vs the `Succeeded` disc **9.9 / 8.5** — both of those are DISCS or bordered identity chips, not rank chips.
  - Verified after every spelling: contrast census over **872 chip halves on 9 routes × 2 themes × 2 widths**, nothing under 4.5 (the floor is the pre-existing `DEV` chip at 4.71), and **zero** clip/overflow events for the whole rank vocabulary.
  - **THE BORDER STAYS NEUTRAL ON EVERY NON-`env` ROLE.** Identity is a coloured EDGE; rank is a coloured FIELD inside the same `gray-200`/`gray-700` hairline `.chip-value` draws. Rendered with matching teal/blue borders instead, the joined badge reads as two glued boxes and a rank chip becomes indistinguishable in KIND from `[DEV]`.
  - `ExposureBar` was the last holder of the hand-picked pair and is now on the ramp too, so the mint has **one** spelling product-wide. Do not reintroduce a hex literal for it.
- **`.chip`'s `12ch` cap was never twelve characters — it is 8.5.** (2026-09-02, third truncation report in one day: `STAGING 15 BEHI…` on `/versions/<rev>`.) `max-width: 12ch` resolves to **72.25px**; padding + border take 13.8 and one character costs 6.85 (1ch 6.02 + 0.8 letter-spacing), so the word's real budget is **(72.25 − 13.8) / 6.85 = 8.5 characters**. Every nine-character label has always clipped, and the fix had been applied three times as a per-call-site `wide`.
  - The cap is **per KIND of label** now, not per call site. `env` labels are UNBOUNDED (an environment, service or region name) and keep 12ch exactly — every deliberate "NOT `wide`" decision in `Navbar`, `CommandPalette` and `/environments` is byte-identical. Every other role's label comes from a CLOSED vocabulary whose longest member is `NEVER DEPLOYED` (109.5px bare, 123.5 with the tag), so the cap is **`calc(14ch+26px)` = 110.3px**, or `calc(14ch+40px)` when the tag draws.
  - It is **strictly tighter than `wide`**, which is what makes it safe across pages a pass does not own: no call site can render wider than an already-shipped `wide` chip. The `wide`s added for this bug are now redundant, not wrong.
  - A DEV `console.error` fires if a non-`env` label exceeds 14 characters, so the next one is NAMED instead of silently truncated.
  - Verified: every word in the vocabulary (`NEWEST`, `1/15/199 BEHIND`, `UNKNOWN`, `HELD`, `PENDING`, `PINNED`, `UNRELEASED`, `ROLLED BACK`, `NEVER DEPLOYED`, `DIVERGED`) renders unclipped with no horizontal overflow on 9 routes × 1440 and 390.
- **`newest` has ONE tone.** (2026-09-01, tone value superseded 2026-09-02 — see above) The word was printed mint on `/` and `/rollouts` (`rankRole()` → `newest`) and neutral gray on `/environments`, `/envs/<name>`, `/apps/<name>` and `PromotionPipeline` (`role="head"`). Measured canvas-resolved on the running product, the gray spelling sat **4.1°** of hue from `N behind` in light and **2.8°** in dark — i.e. the two members of the rank vocabulary were the same hue — while mint separates them by **81°**. `TONE.head` now resolves to `MINT_QUIET`; the role name survives only because four call sites are in files that pass did not own. **Do not give `head` a value of its own again.** Migrate those call sites to `role="newest"` and delete the entry.
- **A page title that repeats the navbar is a duplicate, not a heading.** (2026-09-01, from the human: *"i think i don't like that we have a title on the page when it's already in the navbar."*) `/apps` now renders an `sr-only` `h1` with the page's rollup in the slot the word held. The test is DUPLICATION, not position: `/envs/<name>` keeps its drawn `h1` because the navbar names the section and the page names the environment. Never delete the `h1` element itself — the skip link and the heading-structure tests need it.
- **`/dependencies` KEEPS its drawn `h1`, and so does every page the navbar does not name.** (2026-09-01) The rule is DUPLICATION, not position, and the navbar is the thing to check — not the assumption that every section is in it. `Navbar.svelte`'s `currentSection` has branches for `/apps`, `/environments|/envs`, `/activity`, `/versions` and `/rollouts|/namespaces` only; everything else falls through to `SECTIONS[0]` (`control`), and the breadcrumb is `{#if currentSection.key !== 'control'}` — not rendered. `/dependencies` is not in `Sidebar.svelte` either, so its `h1` is the page's ONLY visible name. Unvoicing it leaves a graph with nothing saying what it is.
  - **Applied (`sr-only` + rollup in the slot):** `/`, `/apps`, `/versions`, `/activity`, `/rollouts`, `/environments`, rollout detail's `/history`.
  - **Drawn, correctly:** `/dependencies` (navbar is silent), `/envs/<name>`, `/apps/<name>`, `/namespaces/<name>`, `/versions/<rev>`, rollout detail — the navbar names the SECTION and the page names the OBJECT.
- **Unvoicing a title without replacing its TYPE ROLE is a reduction, not a fix.** (2026-09-01) Taking `Apps` out left `/apps` running **16 → 10** where `COMPOSITION-GRAMMAR.md` §6 asks for 24 → 10 — "quieter, flatter, smaller-typed", arrived at by deletion. The replacement is `/activity`'s shape: the rollup's **leading figure at `t-display` (24px)** with the rest of the sentence at `t-dense` on its baseline. Six pages now share it.
  - `/rollouts`' head is **scale and spread** (`15 rollouts in 9 namespaces · 2 clusters`), deliberately NOT the severity partition: `Attention 0 · In motion 0 · … · Steady 12` is already drawn 20px below as the filter pills, and a second object reading the same array is what this page's own rules cut. Everything below y=72 on `/rollouts` is unchanged.
- **A tracked uppercase column-header row is what makes a list read as a spreadsheet.** (2026-09-01, from the human, about the app detail page: *"looks too much like spreadsheet. check where else is this the case."*) Nothing on the reference page has one. Before adding a header row, check whether each cell already names itself — on `/apps` all three did, 16px below. Pair the removal with COMPOSITION (`/apps` gained the two-column layout and the right rail `COMPOSITION-GRAMMAR.md` §7 asks for); a header row deleted and nothing built is a reduction, which is what produced the six rejected pages.
- **A control that only changes what you are looking at is NAVIGATION and must look like navigation.** (2026-09-02, from the human: *"i also don't like this investigate button / choose version that act as if they're doing something smart but are just navigating to a page. i think there's more like that."*) A text link, a row that is already a tap target, a chevron — `.nav-link` in `app.css` is the treatment (14px/500, `.btn`'s vertical padding, transparent underline at rest). A control that changes CLUSTER STATE is an ACTION and earns a `.btn`; a FILLED `.btn-primary` is reserved for the action that changes WHAT IS RUNNING, at most one per page. A control that only changes local view state (disclosure, filter pill, modal opener) is neither and legitimately keeps button chrome.
  - **Before restyling, check whether the control should exist at all.** Most rows and card headers are `.tap-zone`s. A second control inside one, pointing at the SAME destination, is a redundant tab stop — delete it. Five of `/apps`' six `NextStep` variants resolved to `/apps/<name>`, the row's own href, and went; `unpin` survived because `?release=<env>` lands on a dialog the row does not.
  - **Applied (2026-09-02 sweep, everything outside `/apps/**` and `/versions/**`):** `/environments` card footers (**deleted** — `href` was the card header's own `titleHref`) and its banner action; `/envs/<name>` adverse-row `Open` (**deleted** — `href` was the row's own `.tap-link`, and it was the `.btn-primary`), its banner action and its empty-state link; `NextStep` itself (an `href` now renders `.nav-link` and IGNORES `primary`; only the `onclick` branch is a `.btn`) which carries `/activity`'s and the rollout dependencies tab's banner actions with it; `ErrorState` (`Back to …` → link, and `Sign in again` demoted from `.btn-primary` — it reloads the page, it does not change what is running); rollout detail's and `/history`'s own 404 `Back to all rollouts`; `/namespaces/<name>`'s empty state; `+error.svelte`'s three ways out; `ChangeList`'s `See the diff on GitHub` (it was a `.btn` in the error branch and a text link in the success branch — the same URL drawn two ways in one component); `RolloutGrid`'s filled-black `Read the docs`.
  - **`AlertPanel` sets `--nav-link-ink: currentColor` on its `actions` row**, so a link in a banner speaks in the SEVERITY's ink like the `Details` disclosure above it. ⚠️ `currentColor`, NOT `inherit`: a custom property accepts CSS-wide keywords FOR ITSELF, so `--nav-link-ink: inherit` resolves to the empty string and the fallback wins. Measured: the link came out `gray-900` inside an amber banner.
  - **`.nav-link` does not say `color: inherit`, and the first draft's bug is why.** Nothing sets a base ink in LIGHT — only `html.dark` does — so `inherit` walked to the initial value and every banner link computed **`rgb(0, 0, 0)`**. The default is `gray-900` / `gray-100`, the pair `html.dark` already names. Canvas-resolved after the fix: 8.13:1 worst case in light, 9.06:1 in dark, on every surface it ships on.
  - **Deliberately NOT changed: rollout detail's `View on GitHub`.** It is navigation wearing `.btn`, and it is also the control `COMPOSITION-GRAMMAR.md` §5 MEASURED the whole button spec from, on the page the human calls the best in the product. Changing a control's weight there has regressed it before. Left as a named exception, not an oversight.
  - **And when the primary moves, re-derive who gets it.** `/apps/<name>`'s card asserted the filled button by POSITION (`i === 0`). Once `Investigate` stopped being a `.btn`, the topmost row could be a failed deploy with no deployable candidate, and the page's only real action (`Deploy <build>`) rendered secondary. The assertion is CAPABILITY now, not position.
- **A gate correctly refusing a candidate is not a stoppage, and `stuck` may not be spelled over it.** (2026-09-02) `promotionBlock.awaitingApprovalGates` means only *"this gate published an allow-list"*, and the environment controller and the dependency controller both publish one — three of the four gate writers land in that bucket. `blockingStory`'s `story.person` is the classified bucket (a join on the published owner reference). Measured on the live cluster, `hello-frontend-app` reports every gate `passing: true` and `DeploymentBlocked=False`, and `/apps/<name>` was the ONE surface calling it `STUCK` in amber while rollout detail and `/apps` both said *"DEV is waiting on another deploy"*. `stuckFor` narrows `detectStuckPromotion`/`detectStuckBehind` with `story.person.length === 0 && story.unknown.length === 0`; `detectStuck` (baking/deploying past its detector), `Failed` and `diverged` are untouched, because those are wedges whatever the gates say.
- **One row per CAUSE, not one per environment — but only where the row has no action.** (2026-09-02) `Needs you` printed three ~330px rows differing by one environment word, each with its own `!`, its own `STUCK 2d` and its own `Investigate`, for one app blocked on one provider. `tasks` refuses to fold stages because *"a single control over a merged stage row is a destructive action with an ambiguous target"* — that reason does not apply to a `waiting` group, which by definition carries no cluster-mutating control, so those fold. The fold key is the set of `kind|clause|clearsAt` of the gates whose `kind !== 'promotion'`: an environment-controller gate is the PIPELINE, not a cause, and is already drawn as an ordered LINE by `PromotionPipeline`. The environments become the row's SET of chips, in promotion order, each the link to its own rollout.
- **Name the FRONTIER, not the deepest symptom, when the depth is only the pipeline.** (2026-09-02) `blockedEnv` ranked by promotion depth, so it put the app page's one banner on PROD and headlined it *"Two things are holding PROD"* while `/apps` and rollout detail both said *"DEV is waiting on another deploy"*. Tiebreak on the count of `promotion`-kind gates first (fewest = front of the wave); where two environments are blocked independently they both carry zero and the depth rule decides, unchanged.
- **A control that SUMMARISES one object must open THAT OBJECT, not the page that contains it.** (2026-09-02, from the human, about rollout detail's commits rollup: *"this link on rollout page doesn't expand the latest history entry. it should also navigate to it. it's not obvious now when we click the button what changes are for the latest deployment."*) The rollup read `1 commit deployed · +1 −1 · 1 file ›` and pointed at `…/history`, which landed the reader on a list with every row collapsed: a promise of *"these changes"* answered with *"a page that contains them"*.
  - The pattern is a **query param naming the entry**, resolved in an `$effect` off `page.url.searchParams` — `?deploy=<revision>` on the History tab, the same shape as `/apps/<name>`'s `?release=<env>`, the logs tab's `?tab=`, `/activity`'s `?env=`. **Not a fragment**: a hash makes the browser scroll on its own, and on a list that renders after its query resolves that scroll lands at an offset that is wrong 300ms later and then visibly fights the page's own `scrollIntoView`.
  - **Name the entry by a stable key, never by index.** `history[0]` is a different deploy after the next promotion, so `?deploy=0` pasted into a chat opens the wrong one tomorrow. Use `revisionSlug` — 12 characters, the length `version-utils` already derived for URLs — and resolve by prefix. A revision can name TWO entries (a rollback re-deploys a build already in the list); resolve **newest-first**, which is both the safe default and the deploy in effect.
  - **It has to survive a DIRECT load**, not only client-side navigation. Latch on the URL, not on a boolean, and do not latch when the key resolves to nothing — the entry may arrive on the next poll.
  - **Arriving is not the same interaction as clicking.** A link arrival gets `block: 'start'` (at 390 `nearest` moved nothing and the fold sliced the expanded panel), `behavior: 'auto'` (a smooth scroll queued during hydration on a nested scroll container never ran — `scrollTop` stayed 0 for eight frames), and **focus moved onto the row's `.tap-link`**. A click on an in-page chart keeps `nearest`, `smooth` and its own focus. Both `announce()` the result: the thing that changed is 500px down and pixels are not an announcement.
  - **Reuse the two highlight idioms already on the page** — the chart's `selectedEntry` blue border and `app.css`'s `.tap-zone .tap-link:focus-visible::after` ring. Do not add a third.
- **`aria-label` REPLACES an element's text, so a label that names only the destination throws away the fact.** `CommitSummary`'s link announced *"See these commits in the deploy history"* and dropped `3 commits deployed` — the one thing the sighted reader gets. Compose: the element's own words, then the destination.
- When you discover a design constraint from user feedback, add it here immediately without waiting to be asked.

## Rollout list visual treatment

- No thickened or colored card borders. For status severity, use the dot indicator in the group header and the status dot in each row.

## The page container, and the vertical rhythm — one rule, measured

From the human (2026-09-01): *"pages have slightly different content margins so navigating
between pages feels jittery."* Measured at 1440 it was two separate defects.

**LATERAL — one content container for the whole product:**

```svelte
<div class="mx-auto max-w-7xl px-4 py-6 sm:px-6">
```

1280px cap, 24px gutters (16px under `sm`). Content left edge **200px** at 1440 with the
sidebar open, **16px** at 390, on every route. There is exactly **one** documented
exception, and it is not a page: rollout detail's **sticky tab strip** is full-bleed
because it is chrome for the whole pane, the way a browser tab strip is. Its CONTENT is
inside the container like everything else.

- ⛔ `/activity` was `max-w-5xl` — **976px against everyone else's 1216, a 128px jump on
  each side** on entry and exit. A narrower measure is legitimate ONLY when justified by
  LINE LENGTH; nothing on `/activity` is prose (a time-axis chart that wants more room, and
  three-column event rows whose right column was being crushed), so it was habit, not a
  reading measure. Removed rather than documented.
- ⛔ Rollout detail's four tabs had **no wrapper at all** and four different paddings
  (`sm:px-5`, `p-3 sm:p-4`, `p-3 sm:p-5`, none). Its column ran the full width of `<main>`
  and its left edge sat at 196 — a 4px sidestep on entry and an unbounded column on a wide
  monitor.
- **If you add a page, use the recipe above.** A narrower `max-w-*` needs a line-length
  argument written next to it.

**VERTICAL — the head band is chrome and is identical everywhere:**

```
y=0    the container's `py-6`
y=24   THE HEAD ROW — one row: a 24px lead (`t-display`, `t-display-id`, or a 24px
       object name with `leading-[1.15]`) and, on its baseline, the page's rollup at
       `t-dense`.  `flex flex-wrap items-baseline gap-x-2 gap-y-1`, height 28px.
y=52   `mb-5` — 20px, never `mb-4` or `mb-6`
y=72   THE FIRST CONTENT ELEMENT, on every page.
```

Only genuine CONTENT may push a page below y=72 — a banner, a filter bar, a definition
sentence long enough to wrap. Chrome may not. Before this rule the first content element
ranged **62 → 98** at 1440 on pages with nothing above it; it is 72 on all of them now.
`/` is the one page with no head band at all (standing constraint: it does not change
visually) — its first ink is still at y=24.

At 390 the head row WRAPS, so its height is set by the rollup's own length. That is content,
not chrome: the 24px above it and the 20px below it are identical at every width.
